reason: This passage from 1 Samuel 14 presents a cautionary tale of failed leadership rather than a model for good leadership. King Saul makes an unwise oath forbidding the people to eat until evening without consulting them or considering their welfare. When the consequences become apparent (the weakened army goes hungry out of fear of his oath), Saul shows no accountability or responsibility for the damage his decision caused. Instead, he attempts to execute his own son Jonathan through a casting of lots to maintain the oath, demonstrating a failure to prioritize his people's welfare. The people themselves must rescue Jonathan and acknowledge his superior leadership, while Saul's actions illustrate the absence of responsible, accountable leadership.
